JUDGMENT
This petition is filed under Section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation of Rs.3,00,000/ along with interest and costs.

2. The facts leading to the filing of the top noted petition are that on 08.11.2019 at about 1.45 p.m,
when the petitioner was travelling in a Tata Bolt XM car bearing SCCH-23 Reg.No.KA660736 in front of Srinidhi Hotel situated on Bengaluru - Tumkur road (NH48), Nelamangala Taluk,
Bengaluru District, at that time a container lorry bearing Reg.No.HR47D9817 which was being driven by its driver in a rash & negligent manner came and dashed against his car.
Due to the terrific impact the Tata Bolt XM car got damaged.

As such the petitioner got it repaired at Noor Car Care,
Tiptur by spending a sum of Rs.38,800/ towards repair charges.
The respondents being the owner and insurer of container lorry bearing Reg.No.HR47D9817 are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 filed written statement denying the petition averments in toto.
However he specifically contended that the container lorry bearing Reg.No.HR47D9817 was duly insured with the second respondent and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, if any, so awarded.

Stating so,
prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
4. The respondent No.2 filed written statement admitting the issuance of policy in respect of lorry bearing Reg.No.HR47D9817.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured lorry is SCCH-23 denied by this respondent.
Rest of the petition averments are also repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 08.11.2019 at about 1.45 p.m., in front of Srinidhi Hotel situated on Bengaluru - Tumkur road (NH48), Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District his car bearing No.KA660736 sustained damages due to the actionable negligence of the driver of container lorry bearing Reg.

2 No.HR47D9817 ?
2.

6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex'sP.1 to 9 were marked on his behalf.
The respondents did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.

Ex. R1  True copy of the insurance policy pertaining to the container lorry bearing Reg.No.HR47D9817 was marked on consent as Ex.R1.
SCCH-23 7.
Arguments were addressed on both sides.
There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident,
they have not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of container lorry bearing Reg.No.HR 47D9817.

With SCCH-23 this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
9. ISSUE NO.2 :
PW.1 has deposed
that in the accident in question his car was damaged and he has spent a sum of Rs.38,800/ towards its repair charges.
At the outset it is worth mentioning that the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he was the owner of Tata Bolt XM car bearing Reg.No.KA660736 as on the date of accident.
In the absence of such proof of ownership of the petitioner over the vehicle in respect of which damages are claimed, the petition itself is not maintainable.
Further survey report is not produced in this case.
This indicates that the petitioner has not chosen to get his vehicle surveyed from an IRDA approved surveyor (in order to assess the actual damage caused to his car).
In support of his claim, the petitioner has only produced Ex.P9 - Bill issued by Noor Car Care, Tiptur.
But the author of the said document is not examined before this Tribunal.

As Ex.P9 is not proved in accordance with law no credence can be attached to the Sri. G.H. Hirannaiah vs ) M/S Mahaveer Transport Pvt. Ltd on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93366918/
3 contents thereof.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this petition, the claimant is claiming special damages which are required to proved like any other claim.
In such circumstances mere production of a document is no proof of the claim at all.

In this regard reliance is placed upon a decision reported in ILR 2000 KAR 2009 between Karnataka SCCH-23 State Road Transport Corporation v/s George Ninum, wherein our Hon'ble High Court has held that : 'Mere production of documents is not sufficient to prove special damages.

entities.text: Karnataka SCCH-23 State Road Transport Corporation v/s George Ninum
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such documents have to be proved.
Mere production of document is not a proof of its contents'.
In the light of the ratio laid down in the decision cited supra the present claim itself is not sustainable.
Therefore in the considered view of this Tribunal, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation.

With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Negative'.
10. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of discussion made supra, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby dismissed.
Parties to bear their own costs.
Draw an award accordingly.
